pathological.Milestone: ⚠ LOWERED a second time, 0.9598 -> 0.9545 (63 files -> 67), and for the same reason as the first: four minimised fuzz reproductions were committed and one of them diverges. The four are the nightly-33148756015 harvest — SK-FUZZ-0009's and SK-FUZZ-0010's, retired out of pathological/open/ now that both are fixed, plus SK-FUZZ-0012's target-typed-new crash and SK-FUZZ-0013's spaced-using arrangement case. ⚠ MEASURED, not assumed: with those four files moved aside the same tree reads 0.9611/0.8889, which is ABOVE the old ratchet — so none of the drop is a formatter regression and all of it is the new fixtures. Three of the four match the oracle byte for byte; blank-line-after-a-trailing-comment.cs is the exception and takes the number down on its own. Its three divergent lines fall in the existing 'wrapping: one side continues where the other broke' class — the oracle breaks after the tuple type and Skala carries `F65 =` onto the first line — which is a phase-3 wrapping disagreement that has nothing to do with the idempotency defect the file pins. ⚠ Dropping it to keep the number is the move this file has already refused once: docs/plan/12 says the corpus only grows, the pathological set exists to hold the files that are hard, and the 330-character delta-debugged case is the entry precisely because the prettier four-line one does not reproduce. Previously: ⚠ The one baseline in this file that has been LOWERED, and the argument is SK-DIV-0018. Six files were added, 54 to 60: SK-FUZZ-0002's, -0003's and -0004's reproductions, SK-FUZZ-0007's pair, and wrapped-file-scoped-namespace-name.cs — the six-line reproduction of the defect that dominated unformatted/scramble, kept here as a named fixture because 204 scrambled files pin it by weight and none of them says what it is. All but one match the oracle byte for byte; mixed-line-endings-after-a-trailing-comment.cs is the exception and takes the number down on its own. That file's three lines are SK-DIV-0018 entire — on a file whose endings are ALREADY mixed the oracle normalises the whole file to one ending and Skala keeps each gap's own, which is what `enforce_line_ending_style = false` says. It is not reachable on any internally consistent file, and crlf-throughout.cs and mixed-crlf-and-lf.cs are both still exact. ⚠ The alternative was to leave the reproduction out of the corpus, and that is the wrong instinct: docs/plan/12 says the corpus only grows, the pathological set exists to hold the files that are hard, and a minimised reproduction dropped because it embarrasses a number is a measurement managing its own result. M10 was 54 files at 0.9636/0.8889.

unformatted/scramble.Milestone: ⚠ 0.6418 -> 0.8900 in one commit (0.8906/0.0263 with symbols supplied; the ratchet reads the bare number): the wrapped file-scoped namespace is fixed. A file-scoped namespace is a MemberDeclarationSyntax, so it owns a continuation frame, and the whole rest of the file is its CHILDREN rather than its siblings - so a wrapped namespace name spent a continuation level that nothing closed until end of file, and every line after it came out +4. VisitFileScopedNamespace now closes it at the `;`, which is VisitChild's existing 'a body indents from its declaration's level' rule applied to the one declaration whose body has no braces. The first measurement predicted 'roughly 0.89' from the 204-file split (0.3800 against the other 176's 0.8893) and that is what it came to: 0.8906, with 84.1 % of the available line gap now closed against 48.3 %. ⚠ Nothing moved on pre-formatted input - constructs 0.9765, real 0.9963/0.9970 - because no file in corpus/real/ has a wrapped namespace name; that is exactly why this survived nine milestones and why the degraded differential was worth building. Pinned by name in pathological/wrapped-file-scoped-namespace-name.cs. First measurement was 380 files at 0.6418/0.0211, null hypothesis 0.3073/0.0000 (corpus/real/'s own, for scale, is 0.9095/0.2684). ⚠ Its own population, beside the corpus/real/ number rather than replacing it. ⚠ RE-MEASURED at the merge of the fuzzer-defect branch.
